findings.F1: The Calmar failed because of one long fall: the book fell 33.7 % over 1114 days, from w1 to its trough in w10, while the coins fell 68.3 %. That fall alone sets the deepest fall against a yearly return of +25.0 %, giving a Calmar of 0.742 against a rule of 0.75.
findings.F2: The book's gain while held depends on the coin's own longer trend. On bars held when the coin's 60-day return was positive, the mean daily gain was +0.219 % (3095 bars, sum +6.79); when it was not, it was −0.020 % (2566 bars, sum −0.51). Above versus below the 50-day average it was +0.209 % (3829 bars) against −0.005 % (2851 bars).
findings.F3: The idea's grading exists only inside a rising 20-day trend. On the 3-day grid among signal cases, the slope of excess return on the forecast is 0.00083 when the 20-day return is positive (1508 cases, forecast-weighted excess +0.65 %). When it is not, the slope is 0.00014 (820 cases, weighted excess +0.14 %).
findings.F4: The weak half of the forecast carries no gain. By forecast quartile, the 3-day excess is −0.17 %, −0.09 %, +0.25 % and +0.96 % (about 712 cases each). With a positive 20-day return, the top half earns +0.66 % (t 2.13, 881 cases) and the bottom half −0.25 % (t −0.92, 627 cases).
findings.F5: Held gain in the losing stretch w1–w10 shows where the fall came from. With the 20-day return at or below zero and a strong forecast, the mean daily gain was −0.045 % (285 bars). With a positive 20-day return and a strong forecast it was +0.075 % (980 bars). In w11–w24, the strong-forecast, positive-trend bars earned +0.582 % a day (1631 bars, sum +9.49), almost all of the book's gain.
findings.F6: The trend condition alone is only part of the 3-day effect, and none of the 9-day effect.
findings.F7: Rebuilt books with costs show how much a trend filter improves the falls.
findings.F8: The idea's size clears the cost. Per case the total move is +0.63 %, 3.3 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade, and the unusual move 1.2 times it. The book's problem is its falls in down-trends, not cost.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 5-day rise, measured in its usual 5-day moves, the more it rises over the next 3 days, only while the coin's 20-day return is positive.
ideas.consequence: A trader holds a coin for three days after a strong 5-day advance only while its last 20 days are up, and stays out of advances inside a falling month, which is where the long fall came from.
ideas.name: five-day rise in uptrend

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 5-day rise, measured in its usual 5-day moves, the more it rises over the next 9 days, only while the coin's 20-day return is positive.
ideas.consequence: A trader holds a strong advance inside a rising month for nine days rather than three, catching the continuation that the trend alone does not give.
ideas.name: five-day rise held longer

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 5-day rise, measured in its usual 5-day moves, beyond its typical 5-day advance, the more it rises over the next 3 days while its 20-day return is positive, with the move growing fastest among the strongest advances.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a rising month puts their size on the strongest advances and treats ordinary advances as no reason to be long, which cuts the deepest fall without losing yearly return.
ideas.name: strong advance in uptrend
